-- Tooltip default colours (VERIFIED, ref-GameTooltip.lua l.3-4). The border is white, the -- background the dark blue tint; applied to the Backdrop in OnLoad exactly as the real -- GameTooltip_OnLoad does (ref-GameTooltip.lua l.79-82). TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_COLOR = { r = 1, g = 1, b = 1 } TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR = { r = 0.09, g = 0.09, b = 0.19 } -- GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor's position math (ref-GameTooltip.lua l.6,73-77): the -- bottom-right screen corner, -CONTAINER_OFFSET_X - 13 in x, CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y in y. DEFAULT_TOOLTIP_POSITION = -13 -- The shopping-compare pair count (ref GameTooltip.lua l.7; PaperDollFrame's listener -- bounds arg2 by it). NUM_SHOPPING_TOOLTIPS = 2
-- "Show Detailed Tooltips" — ref UIOptionsFrame.lua l.100-101, inside UIOptionsFrame_Init: -- SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS = "1"; RegisterForSave("SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS"); -- It is a FrameXML *uvar*, not a CVar, and 1.12 ships it ON — so the detailed second line -- IS the default reference tooltip, not an opt-in. (An earlier note in this corpus had this -- backwards; decision 0661.) The options window's Interface page drives it now -- (decision 1136), and the assignment below is the ONLY statement of the default: the saved -- chunk executes over it at load (1128) and the row captures it as its Defaults value at -- OnLoad — which runs first — so "1" is written down in exactly one place, here. SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS = "1" RegisterForSave("SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS")
-- The bracketed name out of an item hyperlink "|cff…|Hitem:117|h[Tough Jerky]|h|r"; if the -- string has no bracket it is already a plain name (the merchant/loot rows hand plain names). function BenillaTooltip_ItemName(link) if not link then return nil end local _, _, name = strfind(link, "%[(.-)%]") return name or link end
-- Reuse the quality→colour source the loot window already ships (BENILLA_LOOT_QUALITY_COLORS, -- LootFrame.xml — itself matching ui_items.rs quality_color / the client's GetItemQualityColor). -- Unknown/nil quality falls back to common white. All FrameXML files load before any hover -- fires, so the table is defined by the time this runs regardless of file order. function BenillaTooltip_QualityColor(quality) local t = BENILLA_LOOT_QUALITY_COLORS local c = (t and (t[quality] or t[1])) or { r = 1, g = 1, b = 1 } return c.r, c.g, c.b end
-- Copper → "Ng Ms Kc" text for a price/value line (only the non-zero high coins, always the -- copper). math.floor if present, else a truncation fallback. function BenillaTooltip_MoneyString(copper) copper = copper or 0 local mfloor = (math and math.floor) or function(x) return x - (x % 1) end local g = mfloor(copper / 10000) local s = mfloor((copper - g * 10000) / 100) local c = copper - g * 10000 - s * 100 local out = "" if g > 0 then out = g .. "g " end if s > 0 or g > 0 then out = out .. s .. "s " end return out .. c .. "c" end
-- The default anchor (ref-GameTooltip.lua l.73-77, quoted): owner with no auto-anchor, -- then the bottom-right screen corner, above the bag row - CONTAINER_OFFSET_X/Y are the -- manage pass's live values (UIParent.xml). The engine's ANCHOR_NONE drops the previous -- owner anchor (tooltip.rs SetOwner), so no ClearAllPoints - the ref has none either. function GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(tooltip, parent) tooltip:SetOwner(parent, "ANCHOR_NONE") -- Read the two managed globals FRESH, and fall back AT USE rather than assigning a -- copy: this file used to open with `CONTAINER_OFFSET_X = CONTAINER_OFFSET_X or 0`, -- which is a second written statement of numbers UIParent.xml owns. Harmless in the -- shipped load order (UIParent.xml is manifest 42, this file later) but it is the same -- shape as the shadow pair that froze the bag stack at the no-bars corner, so the law -- of 1499 forbids it outright: nothing outside UIParent.xml assigns a managed offset. -- The `or` defaults below cover the tooltip-only harnesses that load no UIParent. local offsetX = CONTAINER_OFFSET_X or 0 local offsetY = CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y or 70 tooltip:SetPoint("BOTTOMRIGHT", "UIParent", "BOTTOMRIGHT", -offsetX + DEFAULT_TOOLTIP_POSITION, offsetY) tooltip.default = 1 end
-- The two-line UI-element tooltip (spec: ref-GameTooltip.lua l.107-123): a white label, -- then the long explanation wrapped underneath in NORMAL_FONT_COLOR — the whole reason a -- 1.12 hover over the ping meter or a micro button is a paragraph and not four words. -- With detailed tips on it seats at the DEFAULT corner, not beside the owner; with them off -- it collapses to the bare label at the owner's right. `noNormalText` says "the explanation -- is the whole tooltip" (the XP bar) — with tips off such a hover shows nothing at all. -- -- Signature note: the ref reads the firing frame from the `this` global; the corpus -- convention is to keep the ref NAME and take that frame as a leading parameter -- (GameTooltip_OnHide(self), GameTooltip_ClearMoney(frame) — same shift). Reference code -- pasted in verbatim must therefore have the owner threaded in as arg 1. -- **The reference's exact signature, because a signature IS api (1199).** Ours used to take -- the owner as arg 1; the reference takes none and reads `this`. Outfitter calls it the -- reference's way (`OutfitterMinimapButton:OnEnter` -> `GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip(text, ...)`), -- so its TEXT landed in our owner slot and `SetOwner` raised -- "bad argument #2: error converting Lua string to table". Found by the use-probe, not by -- reading: it only fires when something hovers. -- -- Our own callers mostly hold the owner in a local that is NOT the firing frame (`bar`, -- `button`, `frame`), so they use the explicit-owner variant below rather than `this`. function GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip(normalText, r, g, b, newbieText, noNormalText) BenillaTooltip_AddNewbieTipFor(this, normalText, r, g, b, newbieText, noNormalText) end
-- The explicit-owner form our FrameXML uses, and where the behaviour above actually lives: -- the owner is threaded in rather than read off `this`. Kept under a Benilla name so it can -- never be mistaken for a reference global an addon might call or replace. function BenillaTooltip_AddNewbieTipFor(owner, normalText, r, g, b, newbieText, noNormalText) -- Detailed tips OFF is the short shape: the label alone, beside whatever it labels. -- A caller that says its label is worthless on its own then has nothing left to show. if SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS ~= "1" then if not noNormalText then GameTooltip:SetOwner(owner, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") GameTooltip:SetText(normalText, r, g, b) end return end -- Detailed tips ON: a paragraph, and paragraphs go to the screen corner instead of -- crowding the thing they explain. GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, owner) if normalText then -- Label in the caller's colour; the explanation under it, wrapped, always in -- NORMAL_FONT_COLOR — the two lines are deliberately not the same colour. GameTooltip:SetText(normalText, r, g, b) GameTooltip:AddLine(newbieText, NORMAL_FONT_COLOR.r, NORMAL_FONT_COLOR.g, NORMAL_FONT_COLOR.b, 1) else -- No label, so the explanation IS the tooltip: it takes the caller's colour, plus -- SetText's alpha and wrap flags (args 5 and 6) — the wrap the second line above -- would otherwise have carried. GameTooltip:SetText(newbieText, r, g, b, 1, 1) end GameTooltip:Show() end
-- ref GameTooltip_OnHide (ref-GameTooltip.lua l.100-104, quoted): the plate colours -- reset for the next owner and the default-corner flag drops. The ref's OnHide also -- hides ShoppingTooltip1/2 - that pair lands with the compare-tooltip slice (0274 P4). -- -- `self or this`: the corpus calls this the REFERENCE way, with no argument at all -- (TipBuddy.xml l.1412, atsw.xml l.3420, and TipBuddy.lua l.2520 which REPLACES the global -- and calls the saved original bare). The signature note above explains the corpus-wide -- shift to a leading parameter; nothing lets us edit an addon, and `this` is exactly what -- the reference reads here, so the two spellings mean the same thing. function GameTooltip_OnHide(self) self = self or this self:SetBackdropBorderColor(TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_COLOR.r, TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_COLOR.g, TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_COLOR.b) self:SetBackdropColor(TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR.r, TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR.g, TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR.b) self.default = nil end
-- The embedded money row — the ref's SetTooltipMoney (ref-GameTooltip.lua l.84-92) over our -- shared coin kit (BenillaMoney_Set, MerchantFrame.xml): a blank line, the coin trio seated -- at the money line's LEFT +4, and the money's width as the tooltip's minimum width. The -- engine fires OnTooltipAddMoney with the computed price (wow-re ui/scratch/tooltip-money.md -- 0x52b650@0x52e376: the engine computes, FrameXML renders) and this is its handler; Lua -- call sites (repair cost) call it directly, exactly like the ref's ContainerFrame does. function SetTooltipMoney(frame, money) frame:AddLine(" ", 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) local numLines = frame:NumLines() local line = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "TextLeft" .. numLines) local coin1 = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "MoneyCoin1") coin1:ClearAllPoints() coin1:SetPoint("LEFT", line, "LEFT", 4, 0) BenillaMoney_Set(frame:GetName() .. "Money", money, true) local width = 4 for i = 1, 3 do local c = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "MoneyCoin" .. i) if c:IsShown() then width = width + c:GetWidth() + 4 end end frame:SetMinimumWidth(width) end
-- The money row clears whenever the content does (the ref wires GameTooltip_ClearMoney to -- OnTooltipCleared; the engine fires it on ClearLines/SetOwner/Hide). BenillaMoney_Clear -- ships in MerchantFrame.xml (the money kit's home) — guard for engine tests that load -- this file alone; in the app every file is loaded. function GameTooltip_ClearMoney(frame) frame = frame or this if BenillaMoney_Clear then BenillaMoney_Clear(frame:GetName() .. "Money") end end
-- The item content channels (SetItemById/SetBagItem/SetMerchantItem/SetBuybackItem) are -- ENGINE methods on the GameTooltip widget (benilla-ui script/tooltip_item.rs, decision -- 0274 P1): one shared renderer — the real client's own shape (0x52b650 behind 8 of the -- 9 Set*Item bindings, wow-re ui/scratch/tooltip-money.md; decision 0126's one-renderer -- law) — over the full item-template store, with the red failed-requirement law and the -- engine-fired sell-price money row (merchant open + real instance + repair off).
-- The reaction color table (ref ReputationFrame.lua l.3-12, quoted) — the unit-name -- recolor's palette; guarded so a later reputation window's own definition wins. FACTION_BAR_COLORS = FACTION_BAR_COLORS or { [1] = { r = 0.8, g = 0.3, b = 0.22 }, [2] = { r = 0.8, g = 0.3, b = 0.22 }, [3] = { r = 0.75, g = 0.27, b = 0 }, [4] = { r = 0.9, g = 0.7, b = 0 }, [5] = { r = 0, g = 0.6, b = 0.1 }, [6] = { r = 0, g = 0.6, b = 0.1 }, [7] = { r = 0, g = 0.6, b = 0.1 }, [8] = { r = 0, g = 0.6, b = 0.1 }, }
-- GameTooltip_UnitColor (ref-GameTooltip.lua l.8-71): creatures color by reaction; -- players read white (the ref's own shipping state — its hostile/PvP player branches -- are the FACTION_BAR_COLORS reds/greens, kept for when PvP states stream). The engine -- prints the name gold and fires UPDATE_MOUSEOVER_UNIT; this recolors line 1 (the -- byte-verified split — the name COLOR is FrameXML's, decision 0276). function GameTooltip_UnitColor(unit) local reaction = UnitReaction(unit, "player") if reaction and FACTION_BAR_COLORS[reaction] then local c = FACTION_BAR_COLORS[reaction] return c.r, c.g, c.b end return 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 end
-- The health bar's own fill colour (spec: ref-HealthBar.lua, the whole file). -- -- Two colourings in one handler. `smooth` asks for the health RAMP — green at the top of -- the range, red at the bottom, and between them a two-segment fade that pins one channel -- at full and slides the other, so the halfway mark reads solid yellow. Without it the bar -- is flat green whatever it reads. Blue is 0 either way, which is what keeps the fade -- inside the red-yellow-green wedge and never lets it wash out. -- -- **Nothing passes `smooth` — not us and not the reference.** Verified: our only caller is -- the status bar's `<OnValueChanged>` below (one argument), and 1.12's own two callers are -- ref-GameTooltipTemplate.xml l.593 and ref-UnitFrame.lua l.181, both of which forward -- `value` alone. So the ramp has never coloured a bar in this game; it is kept because it -- is the contract an addon replacing a unit frame may still call with two arguments. -- -- A value outside the bar's own range leaves the colour untouched rather than being clamped -- to an end of the ramp — the reference's own guard, kept as the reference has it. function HealthBar_OnValueChanged(value, smooth) if not value then return end local bar = this local min, max = bar:GetMinMaxValues() if value < min or value > max then return end local r, g = 0.0, 1.0 if smooth then local filled = 0 if max > min then filled = (value - min) / (max - min) end if filled > 0.5 then r, g = (1.0 - filled) * 2, 1.0 else r, g = 1.0, filled * 2 end end bar:SetStatusBarColor(r, g, 0.0) end
-- `self or this` for the same reason as GameTooltip_OnHide: an addon inheriting -- GameTooltipTemplate re-declares <OnLoad> to add its own line and opens it with the -- reference's bare `GameTooltip_OnLoad();` (TipBuddy.xml l.1402, atsw.xml l.3417) — a nil -- self there is a load ERROR, and the plate it was about to tint never gets its colours. -- The body is the ref's two lines and NOTHING else. It used to end with a `self:Hide()` we -- had added, which the reference (l.79-82, the whole function) does not have — inert for -- our four tooltips, since every one of them carries `hidden="true"` and the loader's -- attribute pass runs Hide() long before OnLoad fires, but NOT inert for an addon: two of -- the 27 declare `hidden="false"` on purpose (PowerAuras.xml l.20, SimpleActionSets.xml -- l.349) and never call Show(), so the extra line hid a tooltip the real client leaves up. -- A helper that quietly does more than the reference's is exactly the kind of thing that -- only shows up when someone else's code calls it. function GameTooltip_OnLoad(self) self = self or this -- The plate colours (ref GameTooltip_OnLoad, ref-GameTooltip.lua l.79-82). self:SetBackdropBorderColor(TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_COLOR.r, TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_COLOR.g, TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_COLOR.b) self:SetBackdropColor(TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR.r, TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR.g, TOOLTIP_DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR.b) end
